LESSON: TIME, DISTANCE AND SPEED

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements 3.3 Mass, Volume, Weight and Density (8 Lessons) • Conversions of u
Topic 3.4: Time, Distance and Speed
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Time, Distance and Speed, part of Measurements 3.3 Mass, Volume, Weight and Density (8 Lessons) • Conversions of u in Grade 9 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we observe speed in daily activities? 2. Why does time vary in different places of the world?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Time, Distance and Speed together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: learner participates in track events to measure speed.

● Digital Literacy: learner uses IT devices to determine time in different zones in the world.

● Citizenship - global citizenship: learner determines local time in different parts of the world.

Values:
● Integrity: learner correctly records individual running time during track events and other games.

● Respect: learner adheres to their lanes on track events and other games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
● Safety: learner observes safety measures and time during games and sports.

● Education for Sustainable Development (ESD): learner participates and chooses careers in games and sporting activities.

● Self-awareness: learner participates and times themselves in games.

Link to other Learning Areas:

Integrated Science: learner uses digital devices such as digital clocks to tell time in different zones of the world.
